archetype.name: Retooling (lost season)
archetype.definition: A team that won 14 and 11 games the last two years and has fallen to a 2-7, bottom-three efficiency team with three different starting quarterbacks, so the rest of the year is about evaluating pieces, not chasing a playoff spot.

report.headline: A recent contender has cratered: no run game, three quarterbacks, no takeaways.
report.take:
Two years ago this was a 14-3 team with the third-best net EPA in the league, and last year it still went 11-6 with a top-10 defense. This year it is 2-7, 31st in net EPA (-0.19) and 30th in offensive EPA, and it hasn't won since the second week. Those two wins, over Washington and Tennessee, both came as a favorite of six or more points and neither covered. That was the first sign the team wasn't what the record briefly suggested. The Eagles have covered once all year, a two-point loss in Jacksonville as a 7.5-point underdog.

The offense is the root of it, and the line is the root of the offense. The Eagles are stuffed on 29.8% of runs, the worst rate in football, and backs gain 2.1 yards before contact (29th), so Saquon Barkley's season is 69 carries in seven games and 3.16 yards a carry as a team. With no run game, a quarterback carousel did the rest: Jalen Hurts started six games, Tanner McKee two, and Joe Milton III got the Week 9 start against the Giants. That game produced -13.5 passing EPA and seven sacks allowed. The 30 sacks allowed rank 30th, and the 36.3% offensive success rate is 31st. The dossier doesn't say why Hurts has been out of the lineup, so the quarterback for the stretch run is an open question.

The defense is less broken than the offense, but it isn't the unit it was in 2024 or 2025. It sits mid-pack in success rate allowed (16th), red-zone touchdown rate (14th) and deep-ball EPA allowed (13th), and it held tight ends well under their norms. What it cannot do is take the ball away: 4 takeaways ranks dead last. A 0.182 pressure rate (26th) and a 30th-ranked QB-hit rate explain much of that, because quarterbacks are rarely rushed into mistakes. Run defense by EPA ranks 31st, which matters a lot this week. A -4 turnover differential and too few drives (31st in time of possession) leave the defense on the field too long.

There is some bad luck in the record. The point differential implies 4.1 wins, not two, and the -2.1 wins over expected ranks 31st. That is a team that should be bad but not this bad. The schedule also softens: Dallas (32nd-ranked defense), Arizona (31st) and Indianapolis (31st offense) come in the next four weeks. A modest bounce to three or five wins is realistic if a quarterback settles in. A return to contention this year is not.

strengths.title: Defense mostly holds its shape
strengths.body: For all the losing, the defense is near league average on a down-to-down basis and doesn't give up many deep shots. It has also kept tight ends quiet. Points allowed rank 18th, much better than the offense, even though the offense keeps putting it back on the field. This holds up as long as the linebackers get healthy; Campbell and Baun are central to it.

strengths.title: Aggressive coaching, steady special teams
strengths.body: Sirianni has gone for it on every fourth-down chance the dossier tracks, the most aggressive rate in the league. That is the right call for a team that struggles to score. Special teams are middle of the pack, so the game doesn't get handed away in the third phase. Neither will carry a bad roster, but both help keep close games close.

concerns.title: The line can't open anything
concerns.body: A league-worst stuff rate and 29th-ranked yards before contact show this isn't a back problem: Barkley is getting hit at or near the line. It also feeds the pass protection, since an offense that can't run faces obvious passing downs. That helps explain 30 sacks allowed and the seven in Week 9. Nothing in the dossier suggests a fix is coming mid-season.

concerns.title: Quarterback carousel, thin receiver room
concerns.body: Three different quarterbacks have started, and the Milton start was the worst passing game of the year. DeVonta Smith (41 targets in four games) and Dontayvion Wicks are both out. That leaves rookie-heavy targets around Makai Lemon and Dallas Goedert. Until one quarterback holds the job, the 27th-ranked pass EPA is likely to stay there.

concerns.title: No pressure, no takeaways
concerns.body: Last in the league in takeaways, with a pass rush that rarely hits the quarterback. Some of that is turnover luck that should tick up. But the 26th-ranked pressure rate is a real cause, not noise. The 6-sack game against the Giants is one game, not yet a trend.

trend.note: Two non-covering wins over weak opponents to open, then a loss every week since. The offense has scored 14 or fewer in three of the last four, and the Week 9 start by a third quarterback was the low point of the passing game.

nextGame.headline: Steelers' top-ranked run game meets the Eagles' softest spot
nextGame.body:
Pittsburgh is a ground team that passes more than it should. It leads the league in run EPA and short-yardage conversion and runs for 5.06 yards a carry. Rodgers' passing has been below average (26th in pass EPA), yet the Steelers sit 3rd in pass rate over expected. Philadelphia's run defense is 31st by EPA, so every time McCarthy hands it off he is attacking the Eagles' weakest unit. On the other side, the Steelers' defense is 6th in EPA allowed, 3rd in sacks and 3rd in red-zone touchdown rate, a bad draw for an offense that can't run or protect. The cracks are tight ends (30th in EPA allowed to TE1) and the deep ball (23rd). The Book has Pittsburgh by 4.5 with a 38.5 total. The early forecast hints at gusty wind and rain showers that could hold totals down further, though it's still days out.

The Eagles come off a bye but stay short-handed: Smith and Wicks out at receiver, Jihaad Campbell out and Zack Baun questionable (back) at linebacker, and Michael Carter II out at corner. Losing two starting linebackers against the league's best run game is the worst possible timing. The dossier doesn't name this week's quarterback. Pittsburgh lost guard Mason McCormick, an every-snap starter now doubtful after what was reported as a significant ankle injury. That is a real dent in its run blocking. Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson could return from injured reserve.

waysToWin.title: Feed Goedert into the soft spot
waysToWin.body: Pittsburgh shuts down WR1s and lead backs but ranks 30th in EPA allowed to tight ends. With Smith and Wicks out, Goedert is the obvious target and the cleanest matchup on the field. Quick throws to him also take pressure off a line facing a top-3 sack defense.

waysToWin.title: Win a low-scoring field-position game
waysToWin.body: Pittsburgh's special teams rank 23rd while Philadelphia's are mid-pack. Sirianni's fourth-down aggression contrasts with McCarthy's caution (31st in go rate). In a game totaled at 38.5, with possible wind and rain, a return or a converted fourth down can decide it.

waysToWin.title: Make Rodgers beat them throwing
waysToWin.body: Pittsburgh's pass game is 26th in EPA and McCormick's absence could blunt the run game. If the Eagles force passing downs, the rush that sacked Milton's counterpart six times last game gets a chance against a 21st-ranked sack rate.

waysToLose.title: Steelers run it down their throat
waysToLose.body: The league's best run offense against a 31st-ranked run defense missing Campbell and maybe Baun. That leads to long drives, a big time-of-possession gap and an Eagles offense that barely touches the ball.

waysToLose.title: Pass rush overwhelms a leaky line
waysToLose.body: Pittsburgh's 26 sacks rank 3rd, and Philadelphia's sack rate allowed ranks 25th. With no run game to slow the rush, obvious passing downs could turn into a repeat of the seven-sack Giants game.

waysToLose.title: Red-zone trips end in field goals
waysToLose.body: The Steelers allow touchdowns on 37.5% of red-zone trips, 3rd best, and the Eagles score 16.4 a game. Settling for threes against a team that wins 80% of its one-score games is a likely losing script.

nextGame.watch: Pittsburgh's early-down runs with McCormick likely out against an Eagles front missing Campbell and possibly Baun: if those runs keep producing, the game is over by the fourth quarter.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect a little better than the first nine games, not a turnaround. The -2.1 wins over expected and 4.1 wins by point differential say some close-game luck should even out, and last-ranked takeaways tend to drift up. Dallas, Arizona, Indianapolis and Houston are all teams with losing records on the slate. What won't regress is the structure: a line that can't run block or protect, and no settled quarterback. Those keep the offense in the bottom few regardless of opponent.

The late stretch of Seattle (5th-ranked defense), San Francisco (8-1, top offense) and a road trip to the Giants is hard. A realistic finish is three to five wins, with draft position and quarterback evaluation the real storylines. Getting Smith, Wicks and the linebackers back helps around the edges.
swingFactors: Who starts at quarterback, and whether he keeps the job
Return of Smith, Wicks, Campbell and Baun

confidence.note: Nine games of consistently poor efficiency, but quarterback uncertainty and a heavy injury list cloud the outlook.
